source: site 43: tools/index_issue.py build --month 2026-11. The lines files in the sales lane (handoff/adlibrary, fit = yes) judged in the month, joined by library id to the mining lane (sources/adlibrary) for search word and start date; days running from its survival.tsv. Keyword sweeps only: ads found by a brand lookup are left out. Counts only: no brand, domain, page name, ad id or quote.

rules_top.name: A line that promises relief from, or names, a disease or a symptom
rules_top.plain: The FDA reads a line that says a product relieves, fixes or prevents a disease or a symptom as a drug claim. A supplement can describe how it supports the body; it can’t say it treats a condition.
rules_top.example: A headline that promises to fix a named gland.

rules_top.name: Proof or ranking words with no basis shown
rules_top.plain: The FTC expects a brand to be able to prove what its words claim. “Clinically proven”, “science-backed”, “best-selling” and “the only” need evidence behind them, and an ad that shows none is flagged.
rules_top.example: An ad that calls its product “scientifically proven” and names no study.

rules_top.name: A line that tells or asks the viewer about their own health
rules_top.plain: Meta’s personal-attributes rule bars an ad that tells or asks the viewer about their own health, with words such as “you have”, “struggling with” or “diagnosed with”.
rules_top.example: A line that tells the viewer they have a named urinary symptom.

rules_top.name: A word that points to a condition, with no rule named
rules_top.short: A condition word, no rule named (FDA)
rules_top.plain: Vera’s word pass flagged a word that points to a health condition, but the judge named no rule for the line, so a person should read it before it leads an ad.
rules_top.example: A line with a symptom word in it that only the word pass flagged.

rules_top.name: The product set beside a prescription drug, a medical device or surgery
rules_top.plain: Naming a prescription drug, a medical device or surgery next to a supplement, or pitching the supplement to people on a drug, reads to the FDA as a disease claim.
rules_top.example: A headline that offers a supplement to people on a weight-loss drug.
